name: Transit Immensus
specific_features: Transits its star every 8.3 standard days, creating regular eclipses for inner planets
description: Transit Immensus orbits close to its parent star on a tight, fast orbit that carries it across the stellar disk every 8.3 standard days, creating regular eclipse events visible from the inner planets. Despite its proximity to the star, the planet's massive atmospheric depth insulates the upper cloud layers from the worst of the stellar heating. Banded circulation patterns drive gases at tremendous speeds, and sub-cloud lightning superstorms produce electromagnetic pulses detectable from across the system.

The dense atmosphere transitions through distinct layers, each with its own chemistry and weather systems. The helium rain separation layer, where helium condenses from the hydrogen atmosphere and falls as liquid droplets, marks the boundary between the outer atmosphere and the deep interior. Above this layer, microbial life exists in floating colonies that ride the atmospheric currents, their simple metabolisms powered by the chemical energy of the atmospheric reactions.

The planet's close orbit and regular transits made it one of the first gas giants discovered in this system, its shadow crossing the star's face visible even to pre-spacefaring civilizations. Ancient records from the system's inhabited worlds reference the regular dimming as a timekeeping mechanism, and some cultures built calendrical systems around the transit cycle. The discovery of microbial life in its atmosphere was one of the earliest confirmations of non-terrestrial biology.

Transit Immensus produces trace amounts of antimatter in its upper atmosphere through interactions between stellar radiation and atmospheric particles, making it one of the few natural antimatter sources known. Collection is extraordinarily delicate work, requiring magnetic containment systems operating in a turbulent atmospheric environment. The antimatter yields are small but the strategic value is immense, ensuring a permanent military and industrial presence in the planet's orbit.
